title-group.article-title: A revision of the Order Tribbulida, with descriptions of new species and clarification of concept boundaries in Tribbulus and allied genera

abstract.p: We revise the fictional Order Tribbulida, describe eight new species, propose one new combination, and clarify concept boundaries for four previously described taxa. A junior synonymy in Tribbulus multiplicans is proposed. The concept of Tribbulus tribbulus is broadened; the concept of Iotageminorius ferrugineus is narrowed. Every datum in this article is fabricated and the subject taxa do not correspond to any real biological entity.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: The Order Tribbulida comprises small spherical organisms distributed across several fictional planetary systems. Earlier treatments (Marbleston 1867, Whittaker 1969, Bergwald 1996) established a baseline classification but left several nomenclatural questions unresolved. Here we address those gaps and describe additional taxa from recently examined material.

sec.title: Materials and Methods
sec.p: Specimens examined are lodged at the Museum of Fictional Taxonomy (MFT), the University of Speculative Zoology Collection (USTC), and the Kronos Herbivore Foundation collection (KHF). Coordinates are omitted; every specimen datum in this study is fabricated.

sec.title: Tribbulus novellus Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov.
Diagnosis
sec.p: Differs from congeners by a uniformly cream-colored pelage and reduced ventral tuft. Reproduction rate approximately half that of T. multiplicans.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4001, adult specimen, Iota Geminorum IV, alpine tundra biome, coll. Faulknerville, no date recorded.

sec.title: Distribution
sec.p: Iota Geminorum IV, alpine biome only.

sec.title: Iotageminorius pallidus Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov.
Diagnosis
sec.p: Distinguished from I. ferrugineus by pale coloration and smaller body size.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4002, adult specimen, Iota Geminorum IV, coastal biome, coll. Ochoa-Renn.

sec.title: Distribution
sec.p: Iota Geminorum IV, coastal biome.

sec.title: Nomenclature
sec.p: Glommivorus glomivorans Coombsworth, 1972: 61 — basionym.

sec.title: Remarks
sec.p: Molecular and morphological evidence places this species within Tribbulus rather than Glommivorus. The genus Glommivorus is proposed as a junior synonym of Tribbulus pending a broader generic revision.

sec.title: Synonymy
sec.p: Tribbulus multiplicans Whittaker, 1969: 236.
Tribbulus fecundissimus Ericksmith, 1974: 88, syn. nov.

sec.title: Remarks
sec.p: Examination of the Ericksmith holotype (KHF-TRB-0331) shows no morphometric separation from Whittaker's type series. We treat the two names as heterotypic synonyms referring to the same concept.

sec.title: Concept
sec.p: We restrict I. ferrugineus to specimens matching Marbleston's original type locality (Iota Geminorum IV, temperate biome). Marbleston's paratype series from Kronos-adjacent systems is here excluded and treated as an undescribed lineage pending a molecular study.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype (fide Marbleston 1968): MFT-TRB-0119.

sec.title: Concept
sec.p: We adopt a broader interpretation of T. tribbulus that includes specimens previously assigned to T. dubius Ericksmith, 1974, based on shared reproductive-rate profiles and pelage micro-structure. The narrower sensu stricto concept is retained for the type-locality population where necessary.

sec.title: Remarks
sec.p: Tribbulus dubius Ericksmith, 1974 is here treated as a junior synonym of T. tribbulus.

sec.title: Concept
sec.p: We follow Hallitonn (2003) in restricting D. rainbowicus to specimens with tetrachromatic iridescence, excluding the dichromatic morph originally illustrated by Bergwald (1996). The excluded morph awaits formal description.

sec.title: Tribbulus multiplicans Whittaker, 1969 — additional synonymy note
Note
sec.p: Some specimens historically referred to Tribbulus dubius Ericksmith, 1974 (particularly the KHF paratype series) show reproductive-rate signatures consistent with T. multiplicans. We propose T. dubius as an additional junior synonym under T. multiplicans for those specimens. This assignment overlaps with the disposition proposed above for the T. tribbulus treatment; the two placements are not fully congruent and reflect two contested interpretations that await further study.

sec.title: Misapplication
sec.p: Recent literature (e.g. Bergwald 2001, Faulknerville 2015) has applied the name X. parasiticus to specimens that differ substantially from Ericksmith's holotype. We treat the recent-literature usage as a misapplication and reserve Ericksmith's name for the type-locality population only. Formal description of the misapplied taxon is deferred pending genetic sampling.

sec.title: Grexinia flava Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov. (montane form)
Diagnosis
sec.p: A yellow-pelaged species from the Cyrus III montane biome. Distinguished from other Grexinia species by a keel-like ventral ridge.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4008, adult specimen, Cyrus III, montane biome, coll. Faulknerville.

sec.title: Grexinia flava Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov. (littoral form)
Diagnosis
sec.p: A yellow-pelaged species from the Cyrus III littoral biome. Distinguished from the montane G. flava above by smaller body size and absence of the ventral ridge. This entry uses the same specific epithet as the preceding treatment in error; correction is pending peer review.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4009, adult specimen, Cyrus III, littoral biome, coll. Ochoa-Renn.

sec.title: Iotageminorius nigrofasciatus Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov.
Diagnosis
sec.p: Dark-banded pelage. Body size intermediate between I. ferrugineus and I. pallidus.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4003, adult specimen, Iota Geminorum IV, canyon biome, coll. Faulknerville.

sec.title: Xenopsyllotribbulus argenteus Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov.
Diagnosis
sec.p: Silver-pelaged parasitic tribble. Cannot reproduce in the absence of a host.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: USTC-TRB-4005, adult specimen, Xelatian IV, associated with T. multiplicans host, coll. Ochoa-Renn.

sec.title: Grexinia cyanella Faulknerville & Ochoa-Renn, sp. nov.
Diagnosis
sec.p: Small blue-pelaged species; the smallest known member of Grexinia.

sec.title: Type material
sec.p: Holotype: MFT-TRB-4010, adult specimen, Cyrus III, deep-forest biome, coll. Faulknerville.

sec.title: Acknowledgments
sec.p: This fabricated monograph exists solely as an assimilate-flow fixture for the hive project. No specimens were examined, no fieldwork was conducted, and no funding was received.
